case_dimensions.name: operation
case_dimensions.why: Different inverse relationships and regrouping logic; multiplying and dividing undo each other as adding and taking away do.
case_dimensions.source: taxonomy section 12; why from section 1

case_dimensions.name: operand_1_digits
case_dimensions.why: Controls magnitude and place-value complexity.
case_dimensions.source: taxonomy section 12; why from section 1
case_dimensions.note: Open-ended: the taxonomy writes the values as '1, 2, 3, 4, ..., N'. Any positive integer is legal; 1 to 4 is what the ladder reaches today.

case_dimensions.name: operand_2_digits
case_dimensions.why: Unequal lengths create alignment errors.
case_dimensions.source: taxonomy section 12; why from section 1

case_dimensions.name: operand_order
case_dimensions.why: For addition, commutativity does not remove the diagnostic value of order.
case_dimensions.source: taxonomy section 12; why from section 1

case_dimensions.name: presentation
case_dimensions.why: Horizontal questions also test conversion and place-value alignment.
case_dimensions.source: taxonomy section 12; why from section 1
case_dimensions.note: assess/tags.py derives only VERTICAL and HORIZONTAL today. STORY and EQUATION_BALANCE are legal values with no generator behind them yet, so no coverage target uses them.

case_dimensions.name: alignment_required
case_dimensions.why: A learner can know the arithmetic but still fail because the shorter number is placed under the wrong column.
case_dimensions.source: taxonomy section 12; why from section 4

case_dimensions.name: regrouping
case_dimensions.why: Separates basic calculation from regrouping: carrying, and exchanging.
case_dimensions.source: taxonomy section 12; why from section 1

case_dimensions.name: regroup_columns
case_dimensions.why: A child may succeed in one column but not another.
case_dimensions.source: taxonomy section 12; why from section 1
case_dimensions.note: Open-ended, and the one dimension whose stored shape differs from its allowed values: assess/tags.py emits a list of column indices counting from 0 at the ones. No coverage target uses this dimension until the report agrees on one representation.

case_dimensions.name: regroup_pattern
case_dimensions.why: Different chains of carries and exchanges expose different misconceptions.
case_dimensions.source: taxonomy section 12; why from section 1
case_dimensions.note: assess/tags.py also emits NONE when no column regroups; that case is carried by regrouping = NONE.

case_dimensions.name: zero_pattern
case_dimensions.why: Zeros change what carrying and exchanging demand.
case_dimensions.source: taxonomy section 12; why from section 1

case_dimensions.name: answer_digit_change
case_dimensions.why: Tests whether the learner anticipates magnitude changes.
case_dimensions.source: taxonomy section 12; why from section 1
case_dimensions.note: assess/tags.py derives SAME, +1 and -1 today; -MULTIPLE and ZERO are legal and unreachable from the current generators, so no coverage target uses them.

case_dimensions.name: num_operands
case_dimensions.why: Three or more addends in the same column can produce a carry greater than 1.
case_dimensions.source: taxonomy section 12; why from sections 2.8 and 5.1
case_dimensions.note: assess/tags.py emits the integer count, so a four-addend item reads 4, not '4+'.

case_dimensions.name: unknown_type
case_dimensions.why: Separates direct computation from reverse reasoning.
case_dimensions.source: taxonomy section 12; why from section 1

case_dimensions.name: unknown_position
case_dimensions.why: Where the blank sits changes the reasoning demand: a missing difference is direct calculation, a missing subtrahend or minuend is inverse reasoning.
case_dimensions.source: taxonomy section 12; why from section 6.3

case_dimensions.name: reasoning_type
case_dimensions.why: Measures calculation, application and reasoning separately.
case_dimensions.source: taxonomy section 12; why from section 1

case_dimensions.name: strategy
case_dimensions.why: Measures strategy choice, not only whether the final answer is correct.
case_dimensions.source: taxonomy section 12; why from section 8

case_dimensions.name: context
case_dimensions.why: Application and operation selection: the operation must be inferred from the situation, not from one keyword.
case_dimensions.source: taxonomy section 12; why from sections 10 and 10.2

case_dimensions.name: taxonomy
case_dimensions.why: Which of the school's two documents a question is a case of: multiplication and division's when any of its operations is × or ÷. A case names its own, so neither document's case holds the other's question.
case_dimensions.source: goals/md1-taxonomy-rows.yaml

case_dimensions.name: digits_max
case_dimensions.why: The longest number's digits.
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: digits_min
case_dimensions.why: The shortest number's digits.
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: answer_digits
case_dimensions.why: How many digits the answer has.
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: answer_zeros
case_dimensions.why: Where the answer's zeros sit: a zero inside an answer (108) is forgotten where one at its end (240) is not.
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: answer_power_of_ten
case_dimensions.why: An answer of exactly 10, 100 or 1000, where every column carries or every place exchanges.
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: answer_round
case_dimensions.why: An answer that is one digit and zeros (100, 1000): every column but the first writes 0.
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: answer_first
case_dimensions.why: The answer written before the sum (□ = 63 ÷ 9): the equals sign read both ways.
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: carry_into_zero
case_dimensions.why: A carry lands on a column where a number shows 0 (208 + 96; 506 × 7).
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: carry_max
case_dimensions.why: The largest carry a column sends on: 3 when four 1-digit numbers are added, 8 in 99 × 9.
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: carry_size
case_dimensions.why: A multiplication's carry of 1, or of more: a carry of 4 is the one a child adds as 1.
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: difference_small
case_dimensions.why: A subtraction across a hundred whose answer is 10 or less (503 − 498).
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: divisor_group
case_dimensions.why: The fact group a 1-digit divisor's table is in: each step of a division is read from that table.
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: equal_operands
case_dimensions.why: The same number twice: a square fact (7 × 7), a number divided by itself (7 ÷ 7).
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: estimate_corrected
case_dimensions.why: A 2-digit divisor whose first estimate, rounded to its ten, must be put right (162 ÷ 18: 20 suggests 8, the answer is 9).
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: exchange_zeros
case_dimensions.why: How many zeros an exchange passes through: 402 − 185 one, 1000 − 476 two.
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: fact
case_dimensions.why: A table fact: two numbers to 12 multiplied, or one read backwards with nothing left over.
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: fact_table
case_dimensions.why: The table a fact is read from: its first number's, or the divisor's.
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: fact_group
case_dimensions.why: The easiest table holding a fact in its first ten rows: the groups the tables are taught in.
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: fact_swapped
case_dimensions.why: A fact whose second number's table is the easier one: the table read the other way (8 × 3).
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: fact_zero
case_dimensions.why: A scaled fact whose own product ends in 0 (50 × 4: 5 × 4 = 20), or a division whose fact uses one of the zeros (200 ÷ 4: 20 ÷ 4).
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: first_digit_smaller
case_dimensions.why: The first digit (or digits) smaller than the divisor, so they join the next: the quotient is a digit shorter.
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: highest_place_reduced
case_dimensions.why: A subtraction whose leading digit lends (105 − 97).
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: knock_on
case_dimensions.why: A carry or exchange that makes the next column need one it would not otherwise have (342 − 148; 18 × 6).
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: method
case_dimensions.why: The way a multiplication or division is worked on the page: the standard ones in a line and in columns, and every method the school's objectives name.
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: missing_count
case_dimensions.why: How many digits are missing.
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: missing_in
case_dimensions.why: Which numbers have a missing digit.
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: missing_place
case_dimensions.why: The place a single missing digit is in.
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: multiplier_zero
case_dimensions.why: A zero in the multiplier: one at its end writes no row (23 × 40), one inside writes none for that place (213 × 102).
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: near_round
case_dimensions.why: A number within 2 of a hundred or 1 of a ten: the one a mental method rounds.
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: one_operand
case_dimensions.why: A 1 among the numbers: × 1 and ÷ 1 leave a number unchanged.
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: partial_products
case_dimensions.why: How many rows a long multiplication writes: one for each digit of the multiplier that is not 0.
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: partial_sum_regrouping
case_dimensions.why: Whether adding a long multiplication's rows carries, once or more.
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: place_value_factor
case_dimensions.why: By 10, 100 or 1000; or a round number, one or both, whose zeros are placed after the fact.
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: planted
case_dimensions.why: The mistake a find-the-mistake question shows, as its misconception code.
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it; multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: quotient_zero
case_dimensions.why: Where the quotient has a zero: the one a child leaves out (612 ÷ 6 = 12).
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: regroup_at
case_dimensions.why: Which places carry (from the ones up) or exchange (from the left), joined: ONES+TENS.
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it; multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: remainder
case_dimensions.why: What is left over: nothing, some, the most a divisor allows, or the whole of a number smaller than the divisor.
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: remainder_use
case_dimensions.why: What a story does with a remainder: drops it, rounds up, asks for it, or asks for both.
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: round_operand
case_dimensions.why: A second number of 10, 100, 1000 or another round number.
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: round_to
case_dimensions.why: The place an estimate rounds to.
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: row_regrouping
case_dimensions.why: Whether a long multiplication's rows carry: none, some or all of them.
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: scaled_fact
case_dimensions.why: A round number's sum that is a table fact once its zeros are off (30 × 4 is 3 × 4).
case_dimensions.source: multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: shape
case_dimensions.why: The shape a kind of question states it printed: an equation's, an estimate's, a fact family's, a multiples question's.
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it; multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: structure
case_dimensions.why: A story's shape, as its template declares it: who joins, shares, groups or compares, and in how many steps.
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it; multiplication & division taxonomy, master tagging matrix, as `md_tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: topic
case_dimensions.why: What an explain-a-claim question is about.
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: unknown_digits
case_dimensions.why: How many digits the hidden number has.
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: zero_operand
case_dimensions.why: A 0 among the numbers.
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: zeros_in
case_dimensions.why: Which numbers have a zero a regroup can pass through.
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it

case_dimensions.name: zeros_max
case_dimensions.why: The most such zeros one number has.
case_dimensions.source: addition & subtraction taxonomy, as `tags.py` measures it
